I don’t buy the spouse argument. Going public like this blows you and your spouse up. Not to mention your family. Just feels unlikely to me. This still feels like another NFL team hit to me.

We extend criminal and civil liability to bartenders who overserve people who later kill others while driving drunk. Why aren’t judges who release violent criminals who then commit murders also held liable by, at a bare minimum, losing their jobs?

I’ve been thinking about this quite a bit as a huge percentage of murders that occur in this country are committed by those with violent records. One argument against it is that judges will be harder to hire, but if they were simply fired I don’t think that’s true. Tons of people want to be judges. It’s a relatively easy legal job that pays decently and gives lawyers control of their schedules and courtroom. Moreover, with the rise of AI legal jobs are getting easier and easier. I’m not sure we

As a general rule, accountability makes people better at their jobs. Right now judges have very limited accountability. If they put their jobs on the line with their criminal court rulings, they would take less risks and more people would stay behind bars. The result seems great.

General rule: if the best thing that can happen for you or your organization is something awful and then you tell us something awful happened, we should be skeptical that the awful thing actually happened.

What does a resolution with Iran look like in my opinion? We get the nuclear dust and a fully open Strait of Hormuz and Iran gets their assets unfrozen & their new leaders are acknowledged as legit. I discussed with @piersmorgan.
